orgs.name: Allies in Healthcare
orgs.purpose: Allies in Healthcare (AHC) empowers students to advance health equity by combining service, advocacy, and education. We provide interdisciplinary opportunities for members to engage with underserved communities, addressing social determinants of health through hands-on projects, outreach initiatives, and awareness campaigns. AHC fosters cultural humility and prepares students to become compassionate, informed leaders in healthcare and beyond. By connecting learning with meaningful action, the organization cultivates a community of students committed to reducing health disparities and creating tangible, positive impacts on both local and broader communities.
orgs.description: Allies of Healthcare is a student-led organization at The Ohio State University that connects healthcare research with meaningful community service. Our goal is to help students explore healthcare beyond the classroom by understanding real-world health challenges and taking action to address them. The organization’s primary focus is student-led research in areas such as public health, epidemiology, healthcare disparities, healthcare access and policy, and community health. Members will work in research groups to investigate healthcare issues, examine existing data and literature, and develop a deeper understanding of how these problems affect different communities. No prior research experience is required—students will have opportunities to learn research skills and collaborate with other students. What makes Allies of Healthcare different is our emphasis on connecting research with service. After identifying a healthcare or public health issue through research, members can participate in relevant volunteering and community engagement opportunities. This creates a cycle of research ? identify a problem ? community engagement ? service ? reflect ? improve research, allowing students to see how what they learn can translate into meaningful action. Whether you are interested in medicine, public health, research, or simply improving healthcare in your community, Allies of Healthcare provides a space to learn, collaborate, serve, and make an impact alongside other students.
orgs.keywords: HealthEquity PreHealth Outreach Volunteer Advocacy Leadership Service PublicHealth OSU Activism

The mission of the organization is to facilitate conversation between opposing political perspectives with the intent to listen and relate rather than to scold or rebuke. In the spirit of the OSU’s mission, we strive to create a culture for our members to be morally responsible political leaders who are able to engage in politics critically, wisely, and skillfully in order to pursue the common good. The organization strives to prepare our diverse student body to be engaged citizens and leaders within our country for the next generation of politics.

orgs.name: Buckeye Bloom
orgs.purpose: At Buckeye bloom, our mission is to cultivate community and awareness around women’s wellness at The Ohio State University. We provide a supportive space where members can grow together through practices that nurture the mind, body, and spirit, including movement, mindfulness, reflection, and self-care. Buckeye bloom exists to empower women with lifelong habits and skills that promote holistic well-being, personal growth, and balance during their college experience and beyond.In alignment with The Ohio State University’s commitment to fostering student success, inclusion, and well-being Buckeye bloom supports the university’s mission by promoting healthy lifestyles, meaningful connections, and personal development. Through intentional wellness programming and community engagement, our organization enhances the overall student experience and contributes to a healthier, more resilient Buckeye community.
orgs.description: College is busy. Wellness shouldn’t be another thing to stress about. Buckeye Bloom is a community built for students who want to feel good, have fun, and find balance while navigating college life. We’re making wellness more accessible by bringing discounted workout classes, healthy eats, local Columbus businesses, and wellness experiences straight to the Buckeye community. Whether you’re looking for a new workout buddy, want to try a fitness class without breaking the bank, need a healthier study-break spot, or simply want to meet people who share your interest in living well, Buckeye Bloom is for you. We believe wellness doesn’t have to mean waking up at 5 a.m. or following a perfect routine. It can be grabbing a nutritious meal with friends, trying something new, taking a break from studying, or finding a community that motivates you to take care of yourself. Our goal? Make wellness fun, affordable, social, and realistic for college students—and help it bloom across campus. Come bloom with us.
orgs.keywords: Wellness health fitness nutrition meditation beauty confidence habits community

orgs.name: Engineers Without Borders at The Ohio State University
orgs.purpose: Engineers Without Borders (EWB) is an international organization that applies engineering solutions to aid in the development of underprivileged communities through community-centered design. EWB-OSU provides professional development, real world engineering service projects, and networking to its members. Internationally, we are working in the village of N'jau, The Gambia and are currently designing a marketplace structure for the women of the village to sell their goods. Additionally, we are in the monitoring and evaluation phase of a structural project in Carrera, Ecuador to improve educational infrastructure. Our chapter traveled to Ecuador last summer and plans on continuing to travel at least once a year to evaluate the finished project. Our local projects teams work with a variety of organizations in central Ohio including South Side Family Farms, SE Urban Farms, and the OSU Psychology Department. Local projects provides many opportunities for hands-on experiences in our own community, including through the many volunteering events we host every semester. Current local projects include designing and producing accessible bilateral stimulation tappers, designing a community garden for South Side Family Farms, and designing and implementing an irrigation system for SE Urban Farms. Our fundraising, marketing, and social teams work to provide funding for our projects as well as keep our members excited and engaged.

orgs.name: FemSTEM
orgs.purpose: FemSTEM is a branch of The Be W.I.S.E Initiative, a 501 (c)3 nonprofit that has inspired 4,860+ women in STEM and has numerous chapters through various districts in Columbus. FemSTEM is a semester-long mentorship program which advocates for supporting and guiding women in STEM through their journey. FemSTEM pairs a high school student with a college student to foster a sisterly bond that will guide the mentee through the demanding process of navigating STEM-oriented career paths. Mentees will work with their mentors to complete a semester-long capstone project in areas of college readiness, professional development, career exploration, personal investigation or community service. Mentors will join a network of fellow college students dedicated to sharing their excitement for STEM, knowledge and connections with their mentees. Creating an individualized and unique plan of action for each mentee depending on their passions, FemSTEM will connect women with a multitude of opportunities such as internships, research, volunteering, jobs, networking, etc. Mentorship is a necessity at any age, and FemSTEM aims to promote mentorship and guidance to young women so they are more than ready to tackle the challenges of college and their career when it's time, as well as building a community of college-aged women in stem.

orgs.name: First-Generation Pre-Physician Assistant Platform
orgs.purpose: Representation matters, and while it is desirable by most to strive to be a flawless Pre-Physician Assistant (PA), undergraduate student, and applicant to Physician Assistant school, it is extremely difficult, especially for those students who are first-generation—a term that is used to describe a person who is the first in their family to break barriers such as finishing high school, attending college, or applying to PA school. Motivated to establish a platform for those who do not have immediate access to a Physician Assistant mentor and those exclusive resources, the “First-Generation Pre-Physician Assistant Platform" is an events based organization, providing our members with monthly meetings focusing on guiding OSU's pre-PA students on the path of success to becoming a Physician Assistant. Our Instagram and GroupMe acts as a 24/7 mentorship service for pre-PA students from Ohio State University and beyond. Answered by well-known, resilient, empathetic, and experienced first-generation certified Physician Assistants, PA students, and PA mentors, this platform will reveal the resources and answers to our most common pre-PA fears, which are usually not posted publicly, as we start our pre-PA journeys. This platform’s hope to assure the spiraling worries of the first-generation pre-PA students and to provide them constant access to pre-PA mentorship that will always alleviate their anxieties throughout their journeys. Creating these collections of resources for these pre-PA communities, this platform will increase the access to the resources and treat the necessity of first-generation pre-PA students having a mentor and community to confide in. There, truly, is no greater feeling–community support is a necessity. So within these platforms, we encourage vulnerable conversation from Pre-PA students, PA-S's, and PA-C’s on their personal, non-traditional, first-generation journeys into the Physician Assistant profession. We are dedicated to bringing attention to these resources in order to increase the number of underrepresented students interested in medicine. By acknowledging the disparities and setbacks that being first-generation has on collegiate students, this organization has proven that what once seemed impossible, is now becoming reality for first-generation students everywhere.

orgs.name: Fostering Brain Health Initiative
orgs.purpose: Our mission is to help children in foster care develop healthy brains and improve their quality of life both short and long term by reducing trauma, providing essential and comfort items, and increasing access to language and communication promoting materials. First, we plan to fundraise and supply resources for emergency evacuation centers to minimize trauma, while providing necessities and comfort items to social workers removing children from homes. Second, we are exploring a partnership to support youth transitioning out of foster care and ensure they have the tools necessary to achieve long-term independence. Third, we want to develop a branch of the club focused on supporting language and communication development among children in foster care. This could include creating accessible resources for foster families and caregivers about supporting language-rich interactions, organizing book or literacy drives, and partnering with community organizations to develop evidence-based activities that promote language development. The initiative could also raise awareness of how disruptions in early experiences and developmental delays may affect children’s opportunities for language learning and communication. We started this organization because we believe children in foster care deserve consistent support, stability, and opportunities to thrive despite circumstances they did not choose. We also want to create a community of students who recognize the long-term impact that early experiences can have on a child’s development and are committed to turning awareness into meaningful action.

orgs.description: Gift of Life at Ohio State is dedicated to helping patients battling leukemia, lymphoma, sickle cell disease, and other blood cancers and disorders find potentially lifesaving stem cell or bone marrow donor matches. Throughout the year, our members host tabling events across campus where students can earn volunteer hours while educating the OSU community about the Gift of Life Marrow Registry and how simple it is to join. By helping more students understand the need for donors and encouraging eligible individuals to register, we work to expand the pool of potential matches for patients searching for their lifesaving donor. Every person who joins the registry could one day be the match a patient has been waiting for. Whether you want to volunteer, educate others, get involved on campus, or join the registry yourself, Gift of Life at OSU gives you the opportunity to make a direct and meaningful impact. orgs.name: GoAERO Sloopy Works
orgs.purpose: The GoAERO (Aerial Emergency Response Operations) team exists to bring together students and professional faculty/staff to design, build, and fly Ohio State’s entry in the international GoAERO Prize. The GoAERO Prize is a three-year global competition with over $2 million in prize money to be awarded, aimed at bringing the world’s brightest minds together to focus on a singular mission: Saving Lives. Teams participating will design and build the first autonomy-enabled Emergency Response Flyer, a high-tech aircraft that will help response teams reach people, places and crises faster and easier than ever before. The Emergency Response Flyer will be a portable aircraft that can be deployed by first responders to natural disasters, medical emergencies and humanitarian crises. We provide an opportunity for team members with a background in aerospace, mechanical, computer science and electrical engineering to demonstrate engineering skills and experiment while solving a societal need. Students can expect to gain knowledge in flight vehicle design, assembly, and testing; technical team building and leadership; time management; and entrepreneurship. At the same time, through this competition, the organization will contribute to the mission of Ohio State in creating and discovering knowledge to improve the well-being of our local, state, regional, national and global communities through life-saving medical/emergency rescue vehicle design.
orgs.description: GoAERO Sloopy Works is a 3-year competition student run organization developing the world's first autonomy-enabled emergency response flyer in the GoAERO competition. We are a multidisciplinary team and have openings to work on mechanical, electrical/avionics, software, powertrain, and business subteams.
orgs.keywords: AEROSPACE ENGINEERING GOAERO VTOL AVIATION

orgs.description: GreekSide is a Christian student organization at The Ohio State University dedicated to building community, fostering meaningful relationships, and encouraging spiritual growth within Greek life. Our mission is to create a welcoming environment where fraternity and sorority members can explore their faith, grow in their relationship with Jesus, and connect with others who share a desire to live out their faith in college. Throughout the academic year, GreekSide hosts large group gatherings, social events, and opportunities for fellowship that bring students from different Greek chapters together. These events are designed to build genuine friendships, encourage conversations about faith, and create a sense of community that extends beyond individual chapters. In addition to our larger events, GreekSide encourages students to become involved in weekly small groups and Salt Company gatherings, where they can develop deeper relationships and continue growing spiritually. We hope to serve as a bridge between the Greek community and other Christian ministries on campus. GreekSide also emphasizes leadership development, intentional mentorship, and service to others. We strive to equip students to positively influence their chapters by demonstrating kindness, integrity, compassion, and Christ-centered leadership. Ultimately, GreekSide exists to help students find authentic community, discover their purpose, and grow in their faith throughout their college experience. Our goal is not simply to host events, but to build lasting relationships and encourage students to make a meaningful impact within their chapters, across Ohio State, and beyond.

orgs.name: Health Education And Development Services for Underprivileged Populations
orgs.purpose: The Health Education Activities and Development Services for the Underprivileged Population (HEADS-UP) works with local non profits and public middle and high schools to develop a sustainable healthcare literacy curriculum for the students attending those schools/programs who are interested in medicine. The purpose of this program is to improve healthcare literacy by means of education, mentorship and resource support for children who are in an educationally, socially and economically disadvantaged position. HEADS-UP will aim to fill the gaps in health education that are not specifically addressed in the school's current academic curriculum. By doing so - we believe that we can establish a pipeline extending from medical school all the way into 1st grade. The mainstay of HEADS UP is our work with Ethiopian Tewahedo Social Services (ETSS), a nonprofit focused on providing services to immigrant and refugee families of Columbus, OH. It is our goal to teach students of the ETSS Youth Summer Program how to build healthy habits that can be applied to their daily life by addressing subjects such as diet and nutrition, exercise, common diseases, and human anatomy. We also hope to provide these students with mentorship (with medical student volunteers) by fostering meaningful and long-lasting relationships through discussion and teaching.

orgs.name: Healthcare Innovation Project
orgs.purpose: The purpose of Healthcare Innovation Project (HIP) is to increase efficiency and reduce costs in the healthcare industry through student-driven entrepreneurship. HIP seeks to provide students with experiential learning opportunities that integrate medicine, business, engineering, and public policy by hosting expert speakers—including physicians, investors, entrepreneurs, patent professionals, regulatory specialists, and financial leaders—and facilitating hands-on programming such as hackathons, pitch competitions, and startup development workshops with professional panels of judges. Through market research, data collection, and mentorship from industry professionals, HIP aims to develop innovative healthcare startup solutions that directly benefit the Columbus community and The Ohio State University campus. By fostering research translation, innovation, leadership development, and community impact, HIP aligns with the mission of The Ohio State University to advance knowledge, serve the public good, and prepare students to become impactful leaders in their professions and communities.
orgs.description: The Healthcare Innovation Project (HIP) explores how innovation happens in healthcare through entrepreneurship, business, and commercialization. Meeting every other week, HIP connects students with expert speakers—including physicians, pharmaceutical executives, healthcare entrepreneurs, academics, and patent experts—to learn how new drugs and medical devices reach patients, how healthcare is financed and reimbursed, and how ideas become real-world solutions. HIP is also developing a healthcare hackathon and pitch competition, where students will tackle healthcare challenges, develop innovative solutions, and present their ideas to a panel of industry experts.
orgs.keywords: entrepreneurship healthcare business medicine technology engineering volunteering hackathon science STEM

orgs.name: Helix Tri-Beta
orgs.purpose: Helix Tri-Beta at The Ohio State University is dedicated to recognizing and supporting students in the biological sciences who are committed to their academic and professional growth. Originally established on campus in 1971 as Helix, the organization was created to foster meaningful connections among biology students while encouraging stronger engagement within the College of Biological Sciences. In 2003, Helix became the Xi Eta chapter of the National Biological Honor Society, Beta Beta Beta (Tri-Beta), expanding opportunities for students to take part in scholarly and professional development within the life sciences. The purpose of Helix Tri-Beta is to cultivate a community of students who are genuinely invested in biology and motivated to deepen their understanding of the field. The organization promotes continued academic engagement and supports involvement in research, while also encouraging thoughtful interaction among students and faculty. Through collaborative events and professional development initiatives, Helix Tri-Beta supports members as they work toward careers in science, medicine, and related disciplines. Beyond its focus on scholarship, Helix Tri-Beta works to strengthen the biological sciences community at Ohio State in a more connected and engaging way. It creates opportunities for students to build relationships, learn from one another, and stay involved outside the classroom. By maintaining an environment centered on growth and collaboration, the organization continues to support student development while contributing to the overall strength of the biological sciences at The Ohio State University.
orgs.description: The organization promotes scholarship in the biological sciences through professional development, research, community engagement, and educational programming. Helix is the Xi Eta chapter of Beta Beta Beta (TriBeta), a national honor society dedicated to promoting research, and academic excellence in the biological sciences. The organization provides opportunities for undergraduate biology students to engage in research, as well as professional development, and provides opportunities to get involved like community service and networking with fellow students and faculty.

orgs.name: Karatedo Doshinkan at Ohio State
orgs.purpose: At the Ohio State University Karatedo Doshinkan, we are committed to preserving and promoting Karatedo's profound legacy and teachings, a martial art with deep roots in the rich history of the Ryukyu Kingdom in Okinawa. Our practice is grounded in the foundational techniques, and Kata passed down by the late Hanshi 10th Dan Ichikawa Isao, embodying the spirit and discipline of our forebears, including the late Grand Master Toyama Kanken. Our dojo is a sanctuary for personal development and physical training, welcoming individuals of all ages and skill levels to explore the depth of Karatedo. Under the guidance of Shihan Dean Lillard, whose dedication to Karatedo has spanned from his university years through leadership roles at Cornell University to his current position at Ohio State, our club aims to foster a community where the harmony of mind, technique, and body is pursued. Through disciplined training, we strive not only for physical robustness and self-defense skills but also for the cultivation of character, aiming to perfect personal virtues in alignment with the core principles of Budo: courtesy, respect, and faith. In embracing the traditional weaponry and kata of Okinawan Kobudo, including the Bo, Sai, Tonfa, Nunchaku, and Nicho-Gama, we connect with the historical essence of martial arts while adapting our teachings to the challenges of the modern world—the legacy of Hanshi 10. Dan Ichikawa Nobuo inspires us to evolve continually, enhancing our students' martial proficiency and personal integrity. At Karatedo Doshinkan at Ohio State, we believe in martial arts as a "business of service," where the pursuit of personal advantage is set aside in favor of cultivating a community of individuals committed to personal excellence and mutual respect. Our dojo is not just a place of physical training; it is a space where we honor our past, challenge our present, and build a legacy for the future, embodying the true spirit of Karatedo for generations to come.
orgs.keywords: Martial arts, fitness, Japanese culture, international organization.

orgs.name: Kensho: Asian Philosophy Reading Group
orgs.purpose: The purpose of the Kensho: Asian Philosophy Reading Group is to create a forum for dialogue amongst advanced undergraduate and graduate students on topics relevant to Asian philosophy. These topics include, but are not limited to, the contributions Asian philosophers have made to the areas of epistemology, ethics, mind, metaphysics, and aesthetics. The Kensho: Asian Philosophy Reading Group aims to provide an environment where members of the Ohio State community are exposed to non-western philosophical thought, come to understand it, and engage in comparative or exegetical work with Asian philosophical thought. It is our belief that having a space to collaborate with our colleagues and peers will generate opportunities for discussions and projects which will advance our understanding of the issues from a non-Western perspective, come to ask new questions that Western philosophical methodologies tend to preclude, and lead to new horizons in philosophical dialogue between the different traditions. In addition, Kensho: Asian Philosophy Reading Group will strive to increase awareness and communication between disciplines, so that students can approach Asian philosophical texts with different methodologies and approaches, leading to a deeper understanding and appreciation for Asian philosophical thought and its varied traditions.
orgs.keywords: Comparative studies, Interdisciplinary studies, Asian Philosophy

orgs.name: Latine Educational Empowerment at The Ohio State University
orgs.purpose: Latine Educational Empowerment is a nonprofit organization that seeks to inform middle and high school Latino students (in regions of Ohio that don’t receive many educational resources) of the educational opportunities at their disposal for college preparation. We aim for current Latino OSU students to meet and discuss ways to better the college path for younger students, amassing advice and experiences that can illuminate a route that often feels nebulous, particularly for Latino youths given the challenges they face compared to their white counterparts. Simply put, this organization will connect current students who have successfully completed the process of college attendance with younger students who may not even be aware of college as a possibility. It will also be a meeting ground for incoming Latino Buckeyes to get better acclimated to campus by meeting current Latino Buckeyes and bond — bond by paying it forward. We will have events that assist Latino Buckeyes of all years and majors to bond with one another as we engage in this mission – events will range from informal discussions and presentations (film, for example) about the position that Latino students occupy within the U.S. education system, our own experiences, and a way forward with those experiences in mind. Our overarching goal is to have at least 2 annual visits (one in fall, one in spring) to The Ohio State University for Latino middle and high school students, with lasting impacts being formed as we inform students of possible collegiate careers.
orgs.keywords: Latinos, Latine, Hispanic, education, service.

orgs.purpose: The purpose of MAS is to develop students into disciplined, acquisition-minded professionals who understand how companies are valued, improved, operated, and acquired. MAS supports the educational mission of The Ohio State University by giving students hands-on experience in the private-company acquisition process, including valuation, sourcing, industry mapping, negotiation, due diligence, transaction structuring, and post-acquisition value creation. MAS focuses on the fields of mergers & acquisitions, private equity, family offices, search funds, entrepreneurship through acquisition, and lower-middle-market company ownership. Members are trained to think like advisors, buyers, and operators. MAS pursues this purpose through technical training, acquisition case studies, live deal simulations, speaker events, alumni engagement, acquisition memo writing, private-company research, and collaborative member projects. MAS is distinct from general finance, paper-portfolio, and stock-pitch organizations. Its guiding principles are: (1) Acquisition over speculation: members study control transactions, not merely price movement. (2) Private markets over public markets: members focus on private businesses, succession opportunities, fragmented industries, and founder-owned companies. (3) Ownership thinking over resume collecting: members learn how a buyer creates value after a transaction closes. (4) Execution over theory: members produce acquisition memos, buyer lists, valuation models, diligence plans, and investment committee presentations. (5) Operators and advisors, not just investors: members learn how bankers, private equity firms, search fund entrepreneurs, lenders, lawyers, accountants, and operators interact in a transaction. (6) Main Street to middle market: members study businesses often overlooked by traditional campus finance clubs, including local, family-owned, and service businesses. MAS shall not operate a paper trading fund as its primary activity, and it does not measure member success by short-term market performance. Success is measured by the quality of a member’s diligence, judgment, written analysis, communication, and ability to understand a business as a potential acquisition target.
orgs.keywords: Finance Private Equity Business M&A Mergers & Acquisitions
orgs.howToJoin: Prospective members submit a written application through the MAS membership form, followed by an interview with members of the Executive Board. Applications are evaluated on interest in M&A and private markets, commitment, and analytical ability. Students from all majors and backgrounds are encouraged to apply.
orgs.joinWhen: Formal recruitment is held during the first few weeks of each fall and spring semester.

However, modesty is often used as an excuse to not workout or be apart of sports due to lack of comfortability and acceptance from society. orgs.purpose: Eating disorders are sadly becoming more and more prevalent, and treatment costs around $30,000 per month, while recovery takes on average 3-5 years. Project HEAL is a national organization that fundraises to provide treatment grants and spreads awareness and body positivity. As a group of Project HEAL Ambassadors at Ohio State, we also help raise money to send eating disorder patients to treatment, therapy, and nutritional counseling. While raising money, we create bonds on campus to encourage, empower, and support one another to have healthy outlooks on our health, our body image, and our lives. We host small and large fundraisers in addition to meeting bi-weekly on campus. This Spring we raised over $3,000 to send eating disorder patients to treatment! We auctioned off raffle items from various businesses in the Columbus community in a virtual and in-person raffle. We are looking forward to hosting our 11th Gala in the spring of 2026! We have so many great things planned for this coming year, and hope you can join us!

orgs.name: Queer Identity in Physics and Astronomy
orgs.purpose: QuiPA exists to foster community, support, and visibility for LGBTQ+ students and allies within the Department of Physics at The Ohio State University. The organization is committed to: • Creating a welcoming and affirming space for LGBTQ+ individuals in physics and related fields; • Building connections through social events, mentorship, and peer support; • Promoting professional development opportunities for LGBTQ+ physicists; • Advocating for inclusive practices and policies within the department and the broader physics community; and • Collaborating with other organizations and departments to advance equity in STEM. QuiPA is open to all students, faculty, and staff regardless of sexual orientation, gender identity, or expression. The organization values collaborative leadership, community-driven decision-making, and a non-hierarchical ethos.
orgs.description: Queer Identity in Physics and Astronomy (QuiPA) is a community for LGBTQ+ students, postdocs, staff, and faculty in the Department of Physics and the Department of Astronomy at Ohio State, along with the allies who support them. We exist because the experience of doing science is never separate from the experience of being a person, and for queer and trans physicists and astronomers, that experience often comes with isolation that goes unnamed. Our goal is simple: to make sure no one in our departments has to navigate that alone. QuIPA offers a space to meet others who share parts of your identity, to talk openly about what it means to be queer in academia, and to build the kind of relationships that make a department feel like home. We host social events and discussions on topics ranging from navigating graduate school and the job market to the history of queer people in science. QuiPA welcomes people of all identities and levels of involvement. Whether you want to come to every event, show up once in a while, or know that a community is here, there is a place for you. You do not need to be out, have everything figured out, or share any particular label to belong. Come say hello; we would love to meet you.
orgs.keywords: Queer, Identity, Physics, Astronomy, Astrophysics, LGBTQ+, Advocacy, Volunteering.

orgs.name: Society for Philosophy of Science
orgs.purpose: The purpose of the Society for Philosophy of Science is to create a forum for discussing issues in philosophy of science. Philosophy of science, as a branch of philosophy, tries to understand the aims, methods, principles, and practices of science. These are investigated both on a general level - by focusing on the topics applied to any branch of science, such as theory and evidence, scientific progress and theory change, confirmation, explanation, etc. - and in a more focused way - by looking into each field of science such as physics, biology, psychology, economics, computer science, etc. Issues closely related to science are also the target of study, such as the relationship between science and policy, moral problems in scientific research and technological advance, feminist science, to name a few. Given the apparent success and a huge impact science has made, understanding science - its nature, role, and value - is undoubtedly an important task. And given that societies are becoming more and more driven by scientific research and findings, the task will also become more and more significant. Society for Philosophy of Science aims to facilitate members of the Ohio State community to engage with the said task. For this, this group will provide various opportunities for people thinking about science to share their ideas and to discuss recent and important works in philosophy of science.
orgs.keywords: Philosophy of science
orgs.howToJoin: Interest in philosophy of science.

orgs.name: Society for the History of Early Modern Philosophy
orgs.purpose: The purpose of the Society for the History of Early Modern Philosophy is to bring together graduate and undergraduate students to freely and rigorously study this period of our shared intellectual lineage, understood roughly as spanning the figures of René Descartes (1596-1650) to Immanuel Kant (1724-1804). As the name suggests, the early modern period has traditionally been understood as the beginning of modern philosophy, as opposed to medieval or ancient philosophy. Many of the questions that dominate this era have a distinctly contemporary flavor in that they have strongly influenced the sorts of problems philosophers continue to study today. These problems include, but are not limited to, the relation of mind to body, the role of a priori reasoning in scientific investigation, the nature of knowledge and our status as knowers, the extent to which the human mind comes already equipped with innate content, and the possibility of rational belief in a divine creator. Thus, this period has unique importance to intellectual historians and contemporary philosophers alike. Additionally, this organization will seek to promote understanding of the field of early modern scholarship by devoting significant attention to secondary literature on these historical figures and problems. In addition to using contemporary scholarship to better understand primary texts and authors, some questions we will focus on include: 1) what is the role that historical scholarship should play in the larger field of academic philosophy? And 2) what historiographical methods should philosopher-historians adopt in their research? It is the belief of this organization that we should seek to understand the ideas and thought processes of those who came before us, both to emulate where they went right and avoid where they went wrong, so that we can together become better inquirers into the truth.
orgs.keywords: philosophy history early modern

orgs.name: Students for Justice in Palestine
orgs.purpose: The Ohio State University Student’s for Justice in Palestine is a democratic student organization, whose main focus is the liberation and self-determinism of the Palestinian people; this includes Palestinians within israel, the Occupied Territories, and diaspora. SJP believes that a crucial step towards a practical political solution relies on justice not only for some, but for all as equal citizens. We condemn israel’s non-compliance with international law. We firmly reject the apartheid system Palestinians in the territories have and continue to live under. We affirm that all peoples are entitled to human rights and the protection of international law. We oppose all forms of racism and xenophobia, including but not limited to, Islamophobia, anti-Semitism, and white supremacy. We oppose all forms of oppression towards marginalized groups globally; particularly we emphasize our solidarity with other oppressed indigenous peoples. We understand that our struggle is inherently linked to a long history of global colonialism, and seek to find association with groups also working for liberation and recognition. We firmly reject the military occupation as well as all other forms of state and institutionalized violence. This includes the blockade on Gaza, and the West Bank Wall. We condemn repression and affirm our right to self-expression; we stand in solidarity with israel’s Palestinian political prisoners who are being unjustly held for doing the same. We insist and that the Palestinian Question be answered with Palestinian self-determinism. We seek to create a dialogue on the Palestinian perspective and encourage all to participate with us. SJP recognizes and supports the 2005 call to boycott, divest, and sanction. BDS should be should be maintained until Israel meets its obligation to recognize the Palestinian people’s inalienable right to self-determination and fully complies with the precepts of international law by: 1. Ending its occupation and colonization of all Arab lands, dismantling the Wall and freeing all Palestinian and Arab political prisoners. 2. Recognizing the fundamental rights of the Arab-Palestinian citizens of Israel to full equality; and, 3. Respecting, protecting and promoting the rights of Palestinian refugees to return to their homes and properties as stipulated in UN General Assembly resolution 194
orgs.description: The Ohio State University Student’s for Justice in Palestine is a democratic student organization, whose main focus is the liberation and self-determinism of the Palestinian people; this includes Palestinians within israel, the Occupied Territories, and diaspora. We aim to raise awareness of the Palestinian liberation movement as well as Palestinian culture as a form of expression and resistance.
orgs.keywords: justice palestine sjp activism student palestinian arab

orgs.name: Talking is Medicine
orgs.purpose: The group Talking is Medicine (TiM) is meant to promote the broader use of psychotherapy techniques in fields of medicine beyond psychiatry. We believe aspects of talk therapies can be applied to the way physicians approach and handle patients in all fields. While medicine as a discipline has been moving towards a more “patient centered” model of care in recent years, we believe doctors can go a step beyond just providing individualized care for physical symptoms. We believe to truly serve our patients, doctors should grow a more profound relationship with them built on empathy and deep, personal understanding. In this way doctors can become more intricately aware of their patients’ needs, allowing them to provide the best in personalized care. TiM aims to provide opportunities for students to learn and practice aspects of different talk therapies and mindfulness in order to improve their ability to connect with, and in extension, treat patients in clinical encounters. Students are also encouraged to come up with other unique ideas related to our mission and execute them through this group. For more information, please email osucomTiM@gmail.com.

Furthermore, it is important to develop the valuable skill of explaining, in an intelligible manner, what one is working on, to intelligent people outside of one’s own discipline. orgs.name: The Federalist Society at The Ohio State University Moritz College of Law
orgs.purpose: The Federalist Society at The Ohio State University is an organization interested in free thought and debate on the current state of the legal order. The Federalist Society is founded on the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to the Constitution of the United States of America, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is—not what it should be. The purpose of The Federalist Society is to promote an awareness of these principles and to further their application through its activities. This requires restoring the recognition of the importance of norms that place a premium on individual liberty, traditional values, and the rule of law among law students, professors, lawyers, and judges. In working to achieve these goals, The Federalist Society will work to create an intellectual network that extends to all levels of the legal community.

It began with a small group from the College of Agriculture and Natural Resources at Michigan State University, who developed opportunities for scholarly achievement in agriculture. In 1986, the group organized its first conference and encouraged other institutions to participate. Since that time, national membership has grown to more than 2,000 students and professionals at more than 50 colleges and universities throughout the United States. Ohio State MANRRS was chartered April 6, 1990 during the 5th national conference of MANRRS. Since that time, chapter membership continues to grow annually. orgs.name: The Running Outreach Initiative
orgs.purpose: The purpose of this student organization is as follows: (1) To expose elementary, middle, and/or high school students, especially those from disadvantaged backgrounds, to the sport of running. This is with the hope of promoting each athlete’s own drive, work ethic, and confidence both inside and outside the sport, as well as presenting a source of camaraderie and physical and mental well-being which they can continue to participate in competitively or as a hobby for the rest of their lives. Healthy lifestyles will additionally be encouraged through talks on nutrition, injury prevention, cross training, and more. The primary route for accomplishing these aims shall be through founding individual running organizations at each school, coached by members of Running Outreach Club with optional support from school staff, which align with that school’s schedule and student availability. (2) To overcome the financial barriers of entry into the sport through extensive fundraising for injury-preventing running shoes and race entry fee payment, and also for community-building running club apparel given adequate funds. External organizations such as running shoe retailers may be partnered with to achieve these ends at a reasonable price. (3) To make an effort to organize races such as 5Ks hosted at partnered schools with the aim of raising money for the school as a whole, providing an outlet through which the athletes can test their newfound fitness without the burden of race entry fees, and bringing together the school’s staff, students, and families as well as the surrounding community with an enjoyable event for all. (4) To, given consent from all athletes and their families at the beginning of the season, capture their endeavors and achievements through a dedicated media effort which produces photos and videos that the athletes and families can look back on proudly long after the season is over. (5) To enhance the cohesion of the coaching staff through a variety of social events in which coaches can build friendships which will positively translate to the administration of running club practices and the community formation in each team as a whole. These events will additionally connect the coaching and administrative staffs, such that coaches shall be acquainted with those supporting their athletes while administrators shall be acquainted with those whose efforts they are supporting.

orgs.name: Zamobuckeyes
orgs.purpose: There is a rich history of collaboration between Zamorano University in Honduras and The Ohio State University (OSU) that includes exchanges of faculty members, visits by researchers, and alumni that pursue graduate studies at OSU. In 2019 a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the two institutions was renewed. Zamobuckeyes is a graduate student organization for Zamorano alumni enrolled at OSU to promote engagement and collaboration with other OSU graduate students that are interested in engaging with the Zamorano and Latin American culture. Zamorano alumni are considered those students who completed their undergraduate and/or graduate education at the Escuela Agricola Panamericana, “Zamorano University” located in Honduras, Central America. The National Zamorano Alumni Association (AGEAP-USA) was established in 1993 and promotes collaboration across disciplines related to agriculture between former graduates and those interested in Latin America and other regions of the world where alumni are located. Currently, it has approximately 450 members from 20 different nationalities in 12 Universities throughout the United States. The purpose of this organization is, but is not limited to, to promote academic, professional, and personal development of its members and foster activities to contribute to the community by sharing interests, ideas, and cultural experiences. Furthermore, this organization aims to promote networking between OSU graduate students, the Zamorano community at OSU, the national Zamorano Alumni Association in the United States, and other organizations interested in the region of Latin America. Zamobuckeyes is a group open to any OSU graduate student interested in understanding and enhancing their connections with international agriculture and Latin American communities. Upper-level undergraduates, especially those considering their path into graduate school, are welcome to apply.
orgs.keywords: Agriculture, Graduate, Student Organization, Zamorano, Alumni, Latin America
